# Code of Conduct

## Our Community

We are building a scientific software project that welcomes contributors of all backgrounds and experience levels. We aim to create an environment where people can collaborate respectfully, learn from each other, and do good science together.

## Expected Behavior

- Be welcoming and inclusive. Treat everyone with respect, regardless of their experience, identity, or background.
- Engage constructively. Disagree on ideas, not people. When you critique code or methods, focus on the technical substance.
- Assume good intent. People make honest mistakes; respond with patience and clarity rather than hostility.
- Give credit fairly. Acknowledge others' contributions, ideas, and inspiration. Cite upstream code and publications accurately.
- Listen actively. Value perspectives different from your own and be willing to update your views based on evidence.

## Unacceptable Behavior

The following conduct is not tolerated in this project:

- Harassment: sustained, unwelcome comments or actions targeting someone based on identity, background, or beliefs.
- Personal attacks: insults, dismissive language, or attempts to undermine someone's competence or character.
- Discrimination: exclusion or prejudice based on race, ethnicity, gender, age, disability, sexuality, religion, or national origin.
- Privacy violations: sharing someone's private information (email, address, phone number, etc.) without their explicit consent.
- Disruption: spam, repeated off-topic messages, or deliberate obstruction of project work.
- Retaliatory action: punishing someone for reporting a concern or participating in an investigation.

## Enforcement

Reports of misconduct should be sent to cooray@stanford.edu with a clear, factual account of what happened, when, and who was involved.

The project maintainer will review reports in confidence, investigate as needed, and respond within one week. Actions taken may include:

- Private conversation with the person in question to clarify expectations.
- Public apology if a breach affects the community.
- Suspension from communication channels or contributions.
- Permanent ban from the project if behavior is severe or repeated.

The maintainer will not disclose the identity of the person who reported the concern unless they consent.

## Scope

This code of conduct applies to all project spaces (GitHub issues, pull requests, discussions, email, chat, in-person meetings) and to public spaces where someone is representing the project or the project's community.

## Attribution

This code of conduct is written in the spirit of the Contributor Covenant (https://www.contributor-covenant.org/), which has inspired codes of conduct across many open-source projects. We have adapted its principles to fit our project's values and culture.
